info.description:
# Introduction
Public REST API for Flood Watch Ongkharak. The Go API is the public backend.

# Evidence and freshness
Keep OFFICIAL, COMMUNITY, and AI provenance distinct.
Availability data that is stale or unavailable is UNKNOWN, never SAFE.

# Authentication
Access tokens use JWT bearer authentication.
Refresh tokens are sent only in an HttpOnly cookie. The cookie uses the configured
SameSite Lax or Strict policy and Secure is enabled in production; refresh tokens
are never returned in response bodies. Phase 2 flood-domain collections are empty
until explicitly populated; no response implies current safe conditions. GUEST has
no persisted role; only USER and ADMIN accounts exist. Authentication is required
for the Phase 1 demonstration routes.

# Community reports
Community reports are always COMMUNITY evidence. Valid submissions and their
images publish automatically while PENDING (not reviewed); VERIFIED means ADMIN
reviewed, not OFFICIAL or SAFE. REJECTED means removed from public access.
Submission time is not a measured observation time. ADMIN removal/restoration
requires a reason and retains history; restoration returns to PENDING.
An ADMIN cannot verify their own report. An empty list never means SAFE.

# Alerts and realtime
Phase 7 alerts are created only by explicit structured rules; no threshold is
preconfigured. Public SSE transports versioned change notifications, not canonical
resource state. Redis outages do not roll back committed PostgreSQL data.

# Errors
Other auth failures use the ErrorResponse envelope (including 403 origin rejection,
415 unsupported media type, 429 rate limiting, and 500 infrastructure failure).

Reconnect with Last-Event-ID (or cursor query in browsers that cannot set headers).

bounded replay; initial subscription begins at the current stream tail.
Heartbeats are SSE comments. Delivery can be duplicated and has bounded retention.
`report.updated` signals creation, edits, image changes, removal and restoration;
refetch canonical REST. It carries only the report ID, never review reasons or
removed content. `report.verified` remains the additional review signal.

Public, fixed-location Open-Meteo model weather, not a station observation,
OFFICIAL flood evidence, or a flood-safety decision. No provider URL or location
override is accepted. Reference coordinates are 14.1 N, 101.0 E, matching the
map center; this is not a district-wide measurement. The API fetches on demand,
caches successful responses for 10 minutes per process, coalesces concurrent
requests, and backs off for one minute after failure. Observations over one
hour old or retained during an upstream outage are STALE; cached evidence over
six hours old is omitted. No cached data or disabled configuration returns 503
with UNKNOWN and null current. Precipitation is over intervalSeconds, not 24h.

get.description:
Public stored CAP read model, separate from app-generated rule alerts.
No upstream HTTP fetch or notification delivery occurs on this request.
Disabled sources return NOT_CONFIGURED and an empty list. Stale or
unconfirmed current evidence is UNKNOWN, never SAFE. Missing feed items
do not erase historical cancellation or imply an all-clear. Pagination
is bounded; histories contain at most twenty newest revisions per item.
The retained read bound is 10000 evidence versions; overflow returns 503
rather than a silently truncated lifecycle. Responses are no-store.
